title: 2025 HMMT February Guts Problem 17
statement: Let \(f\) be a quadratic polynomial with real coefficients, and let \(g_{1}\) , \(g_{2}\) , \(g_{3}\) , ... be a geometric progression of real numbers. Define \(a_{n} = f(n) + g_{n}\) . Given that \(a_{1}\) , \(a_{2}\) , \(a_{3}\) , \(a_{4}\) , and \(a_{5}\) are equal to 1, 2, 3, 14, and 16, respectively, compute \(\frac{g_{2}}{g_{1}}\) .

solutions.text:
We will use the method of finite differences. Define \(b_{n} = a_{n + 3} - 3a_{n + 2} + 3a_{n + 1} - a_{n}\) . Since \(f\) is quadratic, the third finite difference of \(f\) is zero. So, \(b_{n} = g_{n + 3} - 3g_{n + 2} + 3g_{n + 1} - g_{n}\) . Letting the common ratio of the geometric sequence be \(r\) , we get that \(b_{n} = (r^{3} - 3r^{2} + 3r - 1)g_{n}\) . So, \(b_{n}\) is a constant multiple of \(g_{n}\) . Thus the ratio \(\frac{g_{2}}{g_{1}} = \frac{b_{2}}{b_{1}}\) . Computing \(b_{1} = 14 - 3\cdot 3 + 3\cdot 2 - 1 = 10\) and \(b_{2} = 16 - 3\cdot 14 + 3\cdot 3 - 3\cdot 2 = - 19\) , we get

\[\frac{g_{2}}{g_{1}} = \frac{b_{2}}{b_{1}} = \boxed{\frac{19}{10}}.\]
